steps.message:
# RL training run diagnosis

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a historical snapshot: inspect its source,
effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic, logs,
tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an unusual
setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health. A truncated log is not by itself proof of a defect.

Do not launch a full training run, use the network, or modify the historical
snapshot. The dataset, held-out set, model, training-step budget, and evaluation
interval are fixed.

## Deliverable

Write one concise UTF-8 diagnosis to:

```text
$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/agent_answer.md
```

State the verdict, identify the concrete root cause or causes, and explain the
causal chain using specific workspace evidence. Distinguish root causes from
symptoms. Do not propose or implement a fix, and do not write other deliverable
files.
I’ll trace the effective training/evaluation setup to the frozen metrics and logs, then connect any anomaly to its mechanism before writing the verdict.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# GRPO with the DAPO reward manager (overlong buffer penalty) on GSM8K,
3	# Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, veRL 0.8.0, one GPU (FSDP actor + colocated vLLM rollout).
4	# Extra Hydra overrides can be appended as arguments.
5	set -euo pipefail
6	cd "$(dirname "$0")"
7	RUN_NAME=${RUN_NAME:-dapo_gsm8k}
8	MODEL_PATH=${MODEL_PATH:-$PWD/models/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct}
9	RAW_DATA=${RAW_DATA:-$PWD/raw/gsm8k}
10	DATA_DIR=${DATA_DIR:-$PWD/data/gsm8k}
11	OUT=${OUT:-$PWD/results/$RUN_NAME}
12	STEPS=${STEPS:-60}
13	SEED=${SEED:-42}
14	
15	MAX_PROMPT_LEN=${MAX_PROMPT_LEN:-512}
16	MAX_RESP_LEN=${MAX_RESP_LEN:-640}
17	OVERLONG_BUFFER_LEN=${OVERLONG_BUFFER_LEN:-128}
18	OVERLONG_PENALTY=${OVERLONG_PENALTY:-1.0}
19	
20	mkdir -p "$OUT"
21	export PYTHONPATH=$PWD:${PYTHONPATH:-}
22	export WANDB_MODE=offline WANDB_DIR=$OUT
23	export VERL_FILE_LOGGER_PATH=$OUT/metrics.jsonl
24	export TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false
25	python3 data_prep/gsm8k.py --src "$RAW_DATA" --out "$DATA_DIR" 2>&1 | tee "$OUT/data_prep.log"
26	python3 -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \
27	  algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo \
28	  data.train_files=$DATA_DIR/train.parquet \
29	  data.val_files=$DATA_DIR/test.parquet \
30	  data.train_batch_size=64 \
31	  data.max_prompt_length=$MAX_PROMPT_LEN \
32	  data.max_response_length=$MAX_RESP_LEN \
33	  data.filter_overlong_prompts=True \
34	  data.truncation=error \
35	  data.seed=$SEED \
36	  data.dataloader_num_workers=0 \
37	  actor_rollout_ref.model.path=$MODEL_PATH \
38	  actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=True \
39	  actor_rollout_ref.model.enable_gradient_checkpointing=True \

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# GRPO with the DAPO reward manager (overlong buffer penalty) on GSM8K,
# Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, veRL 0.8.0, one GPU (FSDP actor + colocated vLLM rollout).
# Extra Hydra overrides can be appended as arguments.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
RUN_NAME=${RUN_NAME:-dapo_gsm8k}
MODEL_PATH=${MODEL_PATH:-$PWD/models/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct}
RAW_DATA=${RAW_DATA:-$PWD/raw/gsm8k}
DATA_DIR=${DATA_DIR:-$PWD/data/gsm8k}
OUT=${OUT:-$PWD/results/$RUN_NAME}
STEPS=${STEPS:-60}
SEED=${SEED:-42}

MAX_PROMPT_LEN=${MAX_PROMPT_LEN:-512}
MAX_RESP_LEN=${MAX_RESP_LEN:-640}
OVERLONG_BUFFER_LEN=${OVERLONG_BUFFER_LEN:-128}
OVERLONG_PENALTY=${OVERLONG_PENALTY:-1.0}

mkdir -p "$OUT"
export PYTHONPATH=$PWD:${PYTHONPATH:-}
export WANDB_MODE=offline WANDB_DIR=$OUT
export VERL_FILE_LOGGER_PATH=$OUT/metrics.jsonl
export TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false
python3 data_prep/gsm8k.py --src "$RAW_DATA" --out "$DATA_DIR" 2>&1 | tee "$OUT/data_prep.log"
python3 -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \
  algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo \
  data.train_files=$DATA_DIR/train.parquet \
  data.val_files=$DATA_DIR/test.parquet \
  data.train_batch_size=64 \
  data.max_prompt_length=$MAX_PROMPT_LEN \
  data.max_response_length=$MAX_RESP_LEN \
  data.filter_overlong_prompts=True \
  data.truncation=error \
  data.seed=$SEED \
  data.dataloader_num_workers=0 \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.path=$MODEL_PATH \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.enable_gradient_checkpointing=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr=2e-6 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=32 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=32 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef=0.001 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_type=low_var_kl \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.entropy_coeff=0 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.data_loader_seed=$SEED \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.param_offload=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.optimizer_offload=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.name=vllm \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size=1 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.gpu_memory_utilization=0.4 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n=8 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.agent.num_workers=1 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=64 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.do_sample=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=64 \
  reward.custom_reward_function.path=$PWD/reward/gsm8k_reward.py \
  reward.custom_reward_function.name=compute_score \
  reward.reward_manager.name=dapo \
  +reward.reward_kwargs.overlong_buffer_cfg.enable=True \
  +reward.reward_kwargs.overlong_buffer_cfg.len=$OVERLONG_BUFFER_LEN \
  +reward.reward_kwargs.overlong_buffer_cfg.penalty_factor=$OVERLONG_PENALTY \
  +reward.reward_kwargs.overlong_buffer_cfg.log=False \
  +reward.reward_kwargs.max_resp_len=$MAX_RESP_LEN \
  reward.num_workers=1 \
  algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False \
  trainer.critic_warmup=0 \
  trainer.logger='["console","file","wandb"]' \
  trainer.project_name=autorlbench \
  trainer.experiment_name=$RUN_NAME \
  trainer.n_gpus_per_node=1 \
  trainer.nnodes=1 \
  trainer.save_freq=-1 \
  trainer.test_freq=10 \
  trainer.val_before_train=True \
  trainer.total_training_steps=$STEPS \
  trainer.rollout_data_dir=$OUT/rollouts \
  trainer.validation_data_dir=$OUT/val_generations \
  trainer.default_local_dir=$OUT/checkpoints \
  "$@" 2>&1 | tee "$OUT/train.log"

"""Build verl-format GSM8K parquet files from the raw Hugging Face snapshot.

Adapted from verl examples/data_preprocess/gsm8k.py (Apache-2.0); reads the local
snapshot with pandas so the run needs no network.
"""
import argparse
import os
import re

import pandas as pd

INSTRUCTION = 'Let\'s think step by step and output the final answer after "####".'


def extract_solution(answer):
    m = re.search("#### (\\-?[0-9\\.\\,]+)", answer)
    assert m is not None
    return m.group(0).split("#### ")[1].replace(",", "")


def convert(df, split):
    rows = []
    for idx, ex in enumerate(df.to_dict("records")):
        rows.append(
            {
                "data_source": "openai/gsm8k",
                "prompt": [{"role": "user", "content": ex["question"] + " " + INSTRUCTION}],
                "ability": "math",
                "reward_model": {"style": "rule", "ground_truth": extract_solution(ex["answer"])},
                "extra_info": {"split": split, "index": idx, "answer": ex["answer"], "question": ex["question"]},
            }
        )
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--src", required=True, help="raw snapshot dir containing main/*.parquet")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    os.makedirs(a.out, exist_ok=True)
    for split in ("train", "test"):
        df = pd.read_parquet(os.path.join(a.src, "main", f"{split}-00000-of-00001.parquet"))
        out = convert(df, split)
        out.to_parquet(os.path.join(a.out, f"{split}.parquet"))
        print(f"{split}: {len(out)} rows -> {a.out}/{split}.parquet")

import re

_SOLUTION_CLIP_CHARS = 300


def extract_solution(solution_str, method="strict"):
    assert method in ["strict", "flexible"]

    # Optimization: Regular expression matching on very long strings can be slow.
    # For math problems, the final answer is usually at the end.
    # We only match on the last 300 characters, which is a safe approximation for 300 tokens.
    if len(solution_str) > _SOLUTION_CLIP_CHARS:
        solution_str = solution_str[-_SOLUTION_CLIP_CHARS:]

    if method == "strict":
        # this also tests the formatting of the model
        solutions = re.findall("#### (\\-?[0-9\\.\\,]+)", solution_str)
        if len(solutions) == 0:
            final_answer = None
        else:
            # take the last solution
            final_answer = solutions[-1].replace(",", "").replace("$", "")
    elif method == "flexible":
        answer = re.findall("(\\-?[0-9\\.\\,]+)", solution_str)
        final_answer = None
        if len(answer) == 0:
            # no reward is there is no answer
            pass
        else:
            invalid_str = ["", "."]
            # find the last number that is not '.'
            for final_answer in reversed(answer):
                if final_answer not in invalid_str:
                    break
    return final_answer


def compute_score(solution_str, ground_truth, method="strict", format_score=0.0, score=1.0):
    """The scoring function for GSM8k.

    Reference: Trung, Luong, et al. "Reft: Reasoning with reinforced fine-tuning." Proceedings of the 62nd Annual
    Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers). 2024.

    Args:
        solution_str: the solution text
        ground_truth: the ground truth
        method: the method to extract the solution, choices are 'strict' and 'flexible'
        format_score: the score for the format
        score: the score for the correct answer
    """
    answer = extract_solution(solution_str=solution_str, method=method)
    if answer is None:
        return 0
    else:
        if answer == ground_truth:
            return score
        else:
            return format_score

from collections import defaultdict

import torch

from verl import DataProto
from verl.utils.reward_score import default_compute_score
from verl.workers.reward_manager import register
from verl.workers.reward_manager.abstract import AbstractRewardManager


@register("dapo")
class DAPORewardManager(AbstractRewardManager):
    """The reward manager."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        tokenizer,
        num_examine,
        compute_score=None,
        reward_fn_key="data_source",
        max_resp_len=None,
        overlong_buffer_cfg=None,
    ) -> None:
        self.tokenizer = tokenizer
        self.num_examine = num_examine  # the number of batches of decoded responses to print to the console
        self.compute_score = compute_score or default_compute_score
        self.reward_fn_key = reward_fn_key
        self.overlong_buffer_cfg = overlong_buffer_cfg
        self.max_resp_len = max_resp_len

        if self.overlong_buffer_cfg is not None:
            assert self.max_resp_len is not None, (
                f"max_resp_len must be provided if {overlong_buffer_cfg=}, but got None"
            )
            assert self.max_resp_len >= self.overlong_buffer_cfg.len, (
                "max_resp_len must be larger than overlong_buffer.len"
            )
            assert not self.overlong_buffer_cfg.enable or self.overlong_buffer_cfg.len > 0, (
                "overlong_buffer.len must be positive when overlong penalty is enabled,"
                f"but got {self.overlong_buffer_cfg.len}."
                "To disable the overlong penalty, set overlong_buffer.enable = False"
            )

    def __call__(self, data: DataProto, return_dict: bool = False):
        """We will expand this function gradually based on the available datasets"""

        # If there is rm score, we directly return rm score. Otherwise, we compute via rm_score_fn
        reward_from_rm_scores = self._extract_reward_from_rm_scores(data, return_dict)
        if reward_from_rm_scores is not None:
            return reward_from_rm_scores

steps.message: The frozen files reproduce the logged metrics. Validation accuracy rises from 43.82% to 46.47%; response clipping stays low, and the terminal traceback occurs only in Weights & Biases cleanup after the final validation record. I’m now auditing whether the numeric extractor misscores otherwise correct answers.
steps.reasoning_content:
Interesting: acc count vs sum different due bool? At step0 score ones 573 but sum acc 578. Why? likely rows where score non1 but acc1 (overlong correct). Indeed overlong 5 correct => 573+5=578. Good.

Correct clipped 1 at val20 while token count exactly640; could answer at token640 no EOS? If clipped ratio metric valid length==max, regardless actual natural stop exactly max? Could answer complete at token640 but no EOS, possible. Should inspect correct clipped outputs (3 etc), false. DAPO penalty correct output at length exactly640 leads reward0, equal incorrect short => zero advantage group possible. Root cause could be exactly "overlong penalty nullifies correct answer at truncation" but only a few.

Should inspect suspicious reward false positives/negatives. The flexible last number may cause weird. I can programmatically recompute score on full and last300; compare frozen. For all rows score raw = acc - overlong; infer penalty. Check exact matching. Use acc field correctness (0/1) robust. For "false positive" need independently parse final marked answer; if final #### or boxed mismatches gt but acc1, indicates last-number reward overriding explicit final. These matter. Determine counts by step, particularly boxed final extraction. Should have robust parser for \boxed{...} with nested? simple regex numbers within last boxed. For each response:
- all explicit #### final number matches regex "####\s*..." last. Few.
- \boxed{...} many. regex find all `\\boxed\s*\{([^{}]*)\}` and extract numeric last; handle \boxed{\text{...}} maybe.
- final bold `**$18**` not explicit.
Could compare `acc==1` and last explicit boxed numeric exists != gt. If examples. Also `acc==0` with boxed numeric equals gt but last number after box differs -> false negatives due post-answer text. This directly shows last-number bug.
- numeric normalization: exact string mismatches like `18.0` vs `18`, `1,200` vs `1200`, `$` stripped? Flexible not remove commas unlike strict (strict does replace). Many false negatives could be ground truth numeric with representation difference. Since acc0 and final last extracted numeric is equivalent numeric to gt, count. E.g ground truth 1200 and model final `1,200` -> extracted "1,200" != "1200". This is known GSM8K flexible reward issue. How many? Important root cause potentially corrupting reward. Should quantify exact numeric-equivalent false negatives. Also ground truth decimals e.g 6.5, final "6.50" false zero. With GSM8K ground truths integers mostly decimals. Determine `acc==0`, last extracted string numeric canonical equal after commas or float Decimal. Some string invalid ".". Calculate counts. If many, concrete root cause. Validation score could underestimate actual mathematical accuracy; training gets zero for correct formatted numeric answer. But held-out metric `acc` uses same flawed extraction, so actual held-out improvement perhaps more. Does it cause unhealthy training? Only if significant.

Also parser only last300 chars can lose final if long trailing nonnumeric text >300 after response; but no_last300_number near zero, still could last numbers differ. Should have examples.

I'll run comprehensive summary:
- For each step, count `acc` 0/1, reward distribution negative, overlong correct count, penalized correct (positive/negative), truncated correct.
- Canonical false negatives numeric normalization count and examples.
- explicit final mismatch counts for boxed.
- identify output truncation via lengths and ends. Some exactly640 might include EOS? Tokenizer on decoded output excludes EOS so length natural 640? If exact640 no eos, truncated. At l<640 natural.
- correct answers overlong mostly wrong or explicit mismatch.

Use one tokenizer pass maybe 7*1319 + 3*512 = 10k, okay. Could combine all. Output only anomalies.

def _write_generations(inputs, outputs, gts, scores, reward_extra_infos_dict, dump_path, global_steps):
        """Write generation samples as JSONL (runs in background thread)."""
        os.makedirs(dump_path, exist_ok=True)
        filename = os.path.join(dump_path, f"{global_steps}.jsonl")

        n = len(inputs)
        base_data = {
            "input": inputs,
            "output": outputs,
            "gts": gts,
            "score": scores,
            "step": [global_steps] * n,
        }

        for k, v in reward_extra_infos_dict.items():
            if len(v) == n:
                base_data[k] = v

        with open(filename, "w") as f:
            for i in range(n):
                entry = {k: v[i] for k, v in base_data.items()}
                f.write(json.dumps(entry, ensure_ascii=False, default=str) + "\n")

        print(f"Dumped generations to {filename}")

    def _dump_generations(self, inputs, outputs, gts, scores, reward_extra_infos_dict, dump_path):
        """Dump rollout/validation samples as JSONL asynchronously."""
        global_steps = self.global_steps
        future = self._dump_executor.submit(
            self._write_generations,
            inputs,
            outputs,
            gts,
            scores,
            reward_extra_infos_dict,
            dump_path,
            global_steps,
        )
        self._dump_futures.append(future)
        # Clean up completed futures and surface any exceptions early
        still_pending = []
        for f in self._dump_futures:
            if f.done():
                f.result()  # re-raises if the write failed
            else:
                still_pending.append(f)
        self._dump_futures = still_pending

    def _init_dump_executor(self):
        """Create or recreate the dump executor and futures list."""
        self._dump_executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1)
        self._dump_futures = []

    def _shutdown_dump_executor(self):
        """Drain pending dump futures and shut down the executor."""
        for f in self._dump_futures:
            f.result()
        self._dump_futures.clear()
        self._dump_executor.shutdown(wait=True)

def _validate(self, merged: bool = False):
        data_source_lst = []
        reward_extra_infos_dict: dict[str, list] = defaultdict(list)

        # Lists to collect samples for the table
        sample_inputs = []
        sample_outputs = []
        sample_gts = []
        sample_scores = []
        sample_turns = []
        sample_uids = []

        for test_data in self.val_dataloader:
            test_batch = DataProto.from_single_dict(test_data)

            if "uid" not in test_batch.non_tensor_batch:
                test_batch.non_tensor_batch["uid"] = np.array(
                    [str(uuid.uuid4()) for _ in range(len(test_batch.batch))], dtype=object
                )

            # repeat test batch
            test_batch = test_batch.repeat(
                repeat_times=self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.n, interleave=True
            )

            ground_truths = [
                item.non_tensor_batch.get("reward_model", {}).get("ground_truth", None) for item in test_batch
            ]
            sample_gts.extend(ground_truths)

            test_gen_batch = self._get_gen_batch(test_batch)
            test_gen_batch.meta_info = {
                "eos_token_id": self.tokenizer.eos_token_id,
                "pad_token_id": self.tokenizer.pad_token_id,
                "recompute_log_prob": False,
                "do_sample": self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.do_sample,
                "validate": True,
                "global_steps": self.global_steps,
            }
            print(f"test_gen_batch meta info: {test_gen_batch.meta_info}")

            # pad to be divisible by dp_size
            size_divisor = self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.agent.num_workers
            test_gen_batch_padded, pad_size = pad_dataproto_to_divisor(test_gen_batch, size_divisor)
            test_output_gen_batch_padded = self.async_rollout_manager.generate_sequences(test_gen_batch_padded)

            if self.use_rm and "rm_scores" not in test_output_gen_batch_padded.batch.keys():
                # for colocate reward models, we need to sleep rollout model
                # to spare GPU memory for reward model
                self.checkpoint_manager.sleep_replicas()
                batch_reward = self._compute_reward_colocate(test_output_gen_batch_padded)
                test_output_gen_batch_padded = test_output_gen_batch_padded.union(batch_reward)
                # wake up rollout model
                # replace with wake_up method once supported
                self.checkpoint_manager.update_weights(self.global_steps)

            # unpad
            test_output_gen_batch = unpad_dataproto(test_output_gen_batch_padded, pad_size=pad_size)

            print("validation generation end")

            # Store generated outputs
            output_ids = test_output_gen_batch.batch["responses"]
            output_texts = [self.tokenizer.decode(ids, skip_special_tokens=True) for ids in output_ids]
            sample_outputs.extend(output_texts)

            test_batch = test_batch.union(test_output_gen_batch)
            test_batch.meta_info["validate"] = True

            # Store original inputs
            input_ids = test_batch.batch["prompts"]
            # TODO: Can we keep special tokens except for padding tokens?
            input_texts = [self.tokenizer.decode(ids, skip_special_tokens=True) for ids in input_ids]
            sample_inputs.extend(input_texts)
            sample_uids.extend(test_batch.non_tensor_batch["uid"])

            # evaluate using reward_function
            reward_tensor, reward_extra_info = extract_reward(test_batch)

            scores = reward_tensor.sum(-1).cpu().tolist()
            sample_scores.extend(scores)

            reward_extra_infos_dict["reward"].extend(scores)
            for key, values in reward_extra_info.items():
                if key not in reward_extra_infos_dict:
                    reward_extra_infos_dict[key] = []
                if isinstance(values, np.ndarray):
                    reward_extra_infos_dict[key].extend(values.tolist())
                else:
                    reward_extra_infos_dict[key].extend(values if isinstance(values, list) else [values])

            # collect num_turns of each prompt
            if "__num_turns__" in test_batch.non_tensor_batch:
                sample_turns.append(test_batch.non_tensor_batch["__num_turns__"])

            data_source_lst.append(test_batch.non_tensor_batch.get("data_source", ["unknown"] * reward_tensor.shape[0]))

        self._maybe_log_val_generations(inputs=sample_inputs, outputs=sample_outputs, scores=sample_scores)

        # dump generations
        val_data_dir = self.config.trainer.get("validation_data_dir", None)
        if val_data_dir:
            self._dump_generations(
                inputs=sample_inputs,
                outputs=sample_outputs,
                gts=sample_gts,
                scores=sample_scores,
                reward_extra_infos_dict=reward_extra_infos_dict,
                dump_path=val_data_dir,
            )

        for key_info, lst in reward_extra_infos_dict.items():
            assert len(lst) == 0 or len(lst) == len(sample_scores), f"{key_info}: {len(lst)=}, {len(sample_scores)=}"

        if merged:
            print("_merge_validation_results validate result will be merged")
            return {
                "data_sources": data_source_lst,
                "sample_uids": sample_uids,
                "sample_turns": sample_turns,
                "reward_extra_infos_dict": reward_extra_infos_dict,
            }
        data_sources = np.concatenate(data_source_lst, axis=0)
        return self._val_metrics_update(data_sources, sample_uids, reward_extra_infos_dict, sample_turns)

    def _val_metrics_update(self, data_sources, sample_uids, reward_extra_infos_dict, sample_turns):
        data_src2var2metric2val = process_validation_metrics(data_sources, sample_uids, reward_extra_infos_dict)
        metric_dict = {}
        for data_source, var2metric2val in data_src2var2metric2val.items():
            core_var = "acc" if "acc" in var2metric2val else "reward"
            for var_name, metric2val in var2metric2val.items():
                n_max = max([int(name.split("@")[-1].split("/")[0]) for name in metric2val.keys()])

self, batch: DataProto, reward_extra_infos_dict: dict, timing_raw: dict, rollout_data_dir: str
    ):
        """Log rollout data to disk.
        Args:
            batch (DataProto): The batch containing rollout data
            reward_extra_infos_dict (dict): Additional reward information to log
            timing_raw (dict): Timing information for profiling
            rollout_data_dir (str): Directory path to save the rollout data
        """
        with marked_timer("dump_rollout_generations", timing_raw, color="green"):
            inputs = self.tokenizer.batch_decode(batch.batch["prompts"], skip_special_tokens=True)
            outputs = self.tokenizer.batch_decode(batch.batch["responses"], skip_special_tokens=True)
            scores = batch.batch["token_level_scores"].sum(-1).cpu().tolist()
            sample_gts = [item.non_tensor_batch.get("reward_model", {}).get("ground_truth", None) for item in batch]

            reward_extra_infos_to_dump = {
                k: (v.tolist() if hasattr(v, "tolist") else v) for k, v in reward_extra_infos_dict.items()
            }
            if "request_id" in batch.non_tensor_batch:
                reward_extra_infos_to_dump.setdefault(
                    "request_id",
                    batch.non_tensor_batch["request_id"].tolist(),
                )

            self._dump_generations(
                inputs=inputs,
                outputs=outputs,
                gts=sample_gts,
                scores=scores,
                reward_extra_infos_dict=reward_extra_infos_to_dump,
                dump_path=rollout_data_dir,
            )

    def _maybe_log_val_generations(self, inputs, outputs, scores):
        """Log a table of validation samples to the configured logger (wandb or swanlab)"""

        generations_to_log = self.config.trainer.log_val_generations

        if generations_to_log == 0:
            return

steps.message: The evidence supports **unhealthy reward/evaluation**, not an optimization or runtime collapse. The same parser that misscores frozen training rollouts also produces the reported held-out accuracy, so the modest accuracy gain cannot by itself establish a healthy experiment.
steps.reasoning_content:
Defect solid. Perhaps discover root cause includes `extract_solution` clips last 300 chars and exact equality. Root cause at wrapper selecting flexible and underlying stock extractor doesn't normalize. If direct user goal expects "unhealthy" because evaluation invalid due to undercount correct and noisy reward. Should not overstate counterfactual improvement. I can say "UNHEALTHY: reward/evaluation implementation is faulty and gives false negatives/positives, corrupting both training and validation. Runtime/optimizer healthy but cannot rescue validity." Specific chain:
- `data_prep/gsm8k.py:18` strips commas only in ground truth.
- custom reward calls flexible at `reward/gsm8k_reward.py:6`.
- `gsm8k.py:26-27` last 300; `:38-48` finds numeric tokens and takes last; `:65-72` raw string equality.
- For outputs ending `57,500`, GT `57500` mismatch; `28.00` vs `28`; trailing punctuation captured, e.g. rollout step60 row9 `21.` vs GT21 score0. Response-ending units after boxed correct answer mean last numeric token from units (`4 weeks` => 4 vs boxed7) false negative. At step60 23 normalized equivalences zero and 20 boxed correct zero; 8 overlap, 35 unique. At baseline 51 unique. Lower bound corrected metrics if only these are fixed baseline 47.69 and final 49.13, still improves +1.44 vs reported +2.65. Could include "at least 35/1319 = 2.65 pp of final examples are demonstrably false negatives" without suggesting corrected full accuracy exact. Indeed 35/1319=2.6535. The reported final accuracy undercounts by at least 2.65pp (assuming all boxed manually correct? I audited 20 mostly clear; normalized equivalences exact yes, though could earlier reasoning wrong but last number mathematically equals gt is by task ground truth). At step60 normalized 23 + box-only12 = 35. All definite. At baseline 51=3.8666 pp. If include lower bound corrected values, clear these are audits not official, but user says concise and no fix. Better state counts and examples not recompute fix. "The recorded 46.47% is therefore not a reliable measure of mathematical accuracy" is true. "Observed final gain partly reflects scorer behavior" cannot infer exact; I can say reported improvement coexists with defect and cannot validate run. Perhaps mention scorer can also false positives e.g. step1 rollouts row142 final boxed30, GT60 gets1 because response text ends "60 days". This shows training rewards actively wrong in both directions. Very concrete. At step1 there are 21 equivalence false negatives +3 boxed-mismatch false positives. Should get normalized lower bound union at rollouts and false positives counts perhaps enough.
- False negatives at training: step1 21/512 normalized; step30 9/512; step60 11/512. Boxed additional step1 9 marked includes 4 boxed +5 final? Could use conservative equivalence only for all. At step1 three false positives shown.
- These enter same DAPO manager via extract_reward both train/validation, then GRPO advantages, so zero to correct and one to incorrect distort group relative updates. Can assert training impact directly because scoring result assigned token_level_scores and used for GRPO. I can cite `ray_trainer.py:1524-1525`, `:1591` and `dapo.py:102-132`. GRPO uses token rewards to advantage after; no need line exact if concise.
- DAPO overlong is intentional, separate symptom. At validation step0 score0.40085 vs acc0.43821 gap due length penalty. Reconstructed lengths exactly match means within EOS. 640 response, expected 512, 128 buffer. Clipping training 0.59%-5.27%, final2.34%; validation final28/1319=2.12%; baseline39=2.96%. Some correct long answers penalized and a few truncated false positives but small. Is overlong itself a root cause? It adds negative rewards to incorrect lengthy responses, meaning rewards can rank wrong short 0 over correct long negative e.g. correct 640 gets 0, wrong640 -1. But design intentional and modest. User wants distinguish root causes/symptoms. Say "The length penalty explains the auxiliary reward being below accuracy, not the scorer's false negatives. It is an intentional secondary signal, not evidence of collapse." No fix.

- Held-out raw metrics: initial .4382 final .46475, peak step60 .46475 vs step20 .46399 nearly same. Noisy dip .4435 at30. "Small nonmonotonic net gain is a symptom/observation, not proof of health." Training reward fluctuates0.19-0.46, expected with batches. Optimize stable: entropy .388-.598, grad .743-1.052, PPO clip max1.18%, no NaNs, throughput ~9.3k, 19.7-29.3s steps, 60/60 and all eval. End W&B cleanup traceback irrelevant.

arguments.content:
# Verdict: UNHEALTHY — reward and evaluation are corrupted, although execution is stable

**Root cause:** the flexible GSM8K answer extractor is not a valid mathematical-answer comparator. `reward/gsm8k_reward.py:6` selects it; `verl/utils/reward_score/gsm8k.py:26-27,38-48,65-72` searches only the final 300 characters, retains commas/decimal punctuation, takes the last number, and compares raw strings. Meanwhile, `data_prep/gsm8k.py:18` removes commas only from ground truth. Thus equivalent answers receive different strings, and numbers in units or prose after an answer replace the answer itself. The prompt asks for `####`, but the flexible wrapper imposes no such format: at step 60 only 27/1,319 outputs contain `####`, whereas 735 contain `\boxed`, making the last-number assumption especially consequential.

**Observed causal chain:** the same reward manager supplies GRPO training scores and held-out `acc` (`verl/trainer/ppo/ray_trainer.py:675-688,1524-1525,1591`). Consequently, false labels enter group-relative updates and the evaluation metric:
- Final validation has **at least 35 distinct correct answers scored zero**: 23 last-token numerical-equivalence failures plus 12 additional boxed-answer failures after deduplication (51 such cases at baseline). Examples are step-60 row 17, where `$57,500` is scored wrong against `57500`, and row 18, where `\boxed{7}` is followed by “4 weeks,” so `4` is extracted instead. Step-60 rollout row 9 scores `21.` wrong against `21`.
- Training is affected directly: 21/512 step-1 and 11/512 step-60 rollout answers are numerically equivalent to ground truth but receive zero. There are also false positives: step-1 rollout row 142 concludes `\boxed{30}` against ground truth `60`, yet receives accuracy 1 because trailing text ends with “60 days.”

Therefore the reported deterministic held-out gain from **43.82% to 46.47%**, with a dip to 44.35% at step 30, is not trustworthy evidence of health; it is produced by the faulty scorer. Noisy training reward and modest, non-monotonic evaluation are observations, not the root cause.

**Not causal:** all 60 steps and seven evaluations completed. Gradient norms remain 0.743–1.052, entropy 0.388–0.598, and PPO clip fraction at most 1.18%, without NaNs or collapse; throughput is typically about 9,300 tokens/s. Training response clipping is 0.59%–5.27%, final validation clipping is 28/1,319, and aborted/prompt clipping are zero. DAPO’s intentional 512–640-token soft penalty explains why auxiliary reward is below accuracy; it is secondary, not the extraction defect. The sole traceback is Weights & Biases `atexit` cleanup after final metrics and generation dumps (`train.log:1391-1456`), not a training failure.
